title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is seeing a mix of funding boosts and strategic partnerships as nations and companies scramble to enhance their capabilities. Meanwhile, the Pentagon continues to invest in satellite production and resilience amidst rising global tensions.

themes.title: Funding Flows and Startups
themes.body: LegendSpace's recent $29.5 million angel round signals a growing interest in AI-driven propulsion technologies. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's $190 million Series C at a $1.6 billion valuation underscores the bullish sentiment around space startups.

themes.title: International Agreements Gain Traction
themes.body: With Mauritius joining the Artemis Accords, the global coalition for lunar exploration continues to expand. This trend reflects a broader commitment to collaborative space endeavors, even as geopolitical tensions simmer.

themes.title: Military Space Investments Surge
themes.body: The Space Force's tripling of launch contract ceilings highlights the urgent demand for military space capabilities. Coupled with a $1.4 billion boost in the FY27 budget for space resilience, it's clear that defense priorities are shifting upwards.

themes.title: Challenges in Hypersonic Testing
themes.body: The repeated delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests raise questions about the pace of U.S. advancements in this critical area. As other nations push forward, the U.S. may need to reassess its testing strategies to maintain a competitive edge.
